reason: Reviewed as a patch, on today's main, in a throwaway worktree (git worktree add /tmp/dm-review main) rather than from the report — and the patch is closer to landable than three refusals suggest, and further than its author thinks. WHAT HOLDS: the instrument change and its test apply cleanly (git apply --include channels/item_ledger.py --include tests/test_reading_queue_receipts.py: ok) and the ten new tests pass. WHAT STOPS IT, three things, all measured: (1) a regression on main — tests/test_item_ledger_wake_rate.py::TestReadingQueuePrintsTheRate passes 5/5 on clean main and fails 2/5 with the patch, because the receipts split prints each body's rate once in a new per-name block ('desi 1 item(s) 2.0/day, last 4h ago') while the previously landed test asserts it on every item line ('-> desi [2.0/day, last 4h ago]'); both are reasonable and only the author can decide which survives, and a landed test is not mine to delete on his behalf; (2) two append-only hunks no longer apply at all (channels/items.jsonl:6350, to-do-lists/dmitri.md:9 — the files have moved under three days of writes); (3) all four verdict receipts it carries are duplicates of earlier ones: for 20261102T014918Z-555ead87 and 20261102T034925Z-39c75dd8 tarik's verdicts precede them (20261116T050617Z, 20261116T050815Z), and for 20261101T234852Z-e0371554 they CONTRADICT him — tarik recorded postponed at 01:00:21Z, this patch records accomplished at 01:15:34Z, so landing it whole would put two disagreeing verdicts in channels/ledger-verdicts/ with nothing to say which is authoritative. So it cannot land as one patch; it can land as the instrument plus test plus report with the receipts dropped and the two failing tests reconciled, and that is a five-minute edit for the author and a rewrite of his judgement for me. Blocked on Dmitri, not on a reviewer's absence.
